+{
+  "version": "1.1",
+  "assurance": "A3",
+  "requirements": [
+    {"id": "R1", "text": "Extract all access/refresh token creation, parsing, signing, verification, revocation, and lifecycle constants into a dedicated token module."},
+    {"id": "R2", "text": "Add single-use refresh-token rotation with replay detection and token-family revocation."},
+    {"id": "R3", "text": "Replace cookie-backed sessions with bearer JWT access tokens and JWT refresh tokens; login, refresh, and logout expose the new lifecycle without sid cookies."},
+    {"id": "R4", "text": "Rate-limit authenticated requests per resolved user and return an explicit 429 response when that user's quota is exceeded without affecting another user."},
+    {"id": "R5", "text": "Route all protected API endpoints through shared authentication/authorization middleware while retaining the profile, orders, admin, health, and credential behaviors."}
+  ],
+  "tasks": [
+    {
+      "id": "T1",
+      "title": "Dedicated JWT token lifecycle and rotation registry",
+      "deps": [],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R1", "R2"],
+        "criteria": "The token module emits three-segment HS256 JWT pairs through the declared manager interface, rejects malformed/tampered/expired/wrong-type tokens at exact clock boundaries, atomically permits exactly one of simultaneous rotations, revokes all winning-token descendants after replay while preserving unrelated families, and stores only digests plus metadata.",
+        "acceptance_command": "node --test tests/tokens.test.js",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox; no network or socket binding",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "tampered, malformed, expired, and algorithm-confused JWTs are rejected",
+          "an access token cannot be used as a refresh token",
+          "two barrier-released rotations of one refresh token yield exactly one success",
+          "replay invalidates the winner and a later descendant while an unrelated family remains valid",
+          "tokens pass at exp minus one tick and fail exactly at exp",
+          "registry inspection finds digest keys and no raw access or refresh token substring in keys or values"
+        ],
+        "risk": "security and clock/concurrency semantics: refresh rotation must consume the old digest before issuing its replacement, expiration boundaries must fail closed, and raw refresh tokens must not be retained",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine Node test output produced_after_change",
+        "integration_seam": false,
+        "risk_class": "security",
+        "required_verification_tier": "adversarial",
+        "rerunnable": true,
+        "constraints": ["standard library only", "no network", "no plaintext token registry"]
+      }
+    },
+    {
+      "id": "T2",
+      "title": "Shared bearer authentication and per-user rate-limit middleware",
+      "deps": ["T1"],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R4", "R5"],
+        "criteria": "Middleware resolves only valid access bearer tokens to existing users, reloads authorization roles from the user store, authenticates before selecting a quota key, and counts requests in isolated per-user fixed windows with exact boundary and Retry-After behavior.",
+        "acceptance_command": "node --test tests/middleware.test.js",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox; deterministic injected clock and no socket binding",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "missing, malformed, refresh-type, and unknown-user bearer claims are unauthorized",
+          "a validly signed Alice token carrying an admin role claim remains forbidden because stored user role wins",
+          "forged/invalid Alice claims and unauthenticated traffic create no Alice quota state",
+          "one exhausted user's quota does not consume another user's quota",
+          "the final millisecond remains limited, exactly windowMs resets, and Retry-After matches the remaining rounded-up seconds"
+        ],
+        "risk": "security boundary and clock isolation: middleware ordering must authenticate before choosing a rate-limit key, and per-user counters must not become a global denial of service",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine Node test output produced_after_change",
+        "integration_seam": true,
+        "risk_class": "security",
+        "required_verification_tier": "adversarial",
+        "rerunnable": true,
+        "constraints": ["standard library only", "no IP-derived identity", "no network"]
+      }
+    },
+    {
+      "id": "T3",
+      "title": "JWT endpoint migration and full API integration",
+      "deps": ["T1", "T2"],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5"],
+        "criteria": "The declared login/refresh/logout shapes implement the JWT lifecycle without cookies; all three protected routes are constructed through the one shared middleware boundary; the whole suite proves prior token/middleware behavior still holds; architecture checks reject legacy session files, duplicate token logic, inline route authentication, skipped/empty tests, and stale cookie documentation.",
+        "acceptance_command": "./run-tests.sh",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox using an in-process request/response harness because listen(2) is denied",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "legacy sid cookies never authenticate and successful login emits no Set-Cookie header",
+          "replayed or revoked refresh tokens cannot mint access tokens",
+          "unauthorized, forbidden, and per-user over-limit requests return 401, 403, and 429 respectively",
+          "tampered or expired bearer JWTs fail on profile, orders, and admin",
+          "invalid JSON and wrong credentials preserve 400 and 401 behavior; health stays public",
+          "source checks require sessions.js removal, ban cookie/session/Set-Cookie and token lifecycle logic outside tokens.js, and require every protected route declaration to call protectedEndpoint",
+          "test inventory asserts named token, middleware, API, and architecture tests ran so empty or skipped files cannot pass",
+          "one injected fake clock drives issuance, verification, refresh, rate limiting, and the exact integration boundaries"
+        ],
+        "risk": "security integration seam across routing, body parsing, token lifecycle, authorization, rate limiting, and removal of legacy session bypasses",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine full test output and structural README/source search produced_after_change",
+        "integration_seam": true,
+        "risk_class": "security",
+        "required_verification_tier": "adversarial",
+        "rerunnable": true,
+        "constraints": ["standard library only", "no socket binding", "preserve unrelated user/order data"]
+      }
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```

+++ b/.agentfw-plan.md
@@ -0,0 +1,123 @@
+# Authentication refactor plan
+
+## Capability preflight
+
+- Filesystem/permissions: the active session reports workspace-write with approval policy `never`; implementation is limited to this repository. Probe: the session permission profile plus `sed -n '1,240p' ~/.codex/config.toml` recorded the install default for comparison; the active managed sandbox supersedes that default.
+- Shell: active. Probe: `node --version` returned `v25.8.2`; baseline `./run-tests.sh` recorded `listen EPERM 127.0.0.1`, so tests must use an in-process HTTP request/response harness.
+- Isolated agents / independent review: active. Probe: two independent review-only subagents were successfully dispatched and returned separate C0-C5 verdicts.
+- Parallel agents: active, but writers share one worktree; implementation workers are serialized by dependency and path ownership.
+- Persistent state: this plan and test evidence are repository artifacts; no external task store is assumed.
+
+## Design decisions
+
+- Use compact, standards-shaped HS256 JWTs with explicit `access` and `refresh` token types. Access tokens are short-lived; refresh tokens are single-use and rotate into a new pair.
+- Keep refresh-token replay state in a dedicated token registry, keyed by a digest rather than raw token material. Reuse of a rotated token revokes its entire token family.
+- Remove cookie parsing, cookie issuance, and the server-side cookie session store from request authentication.
+- Apply authentication and per-user rate limiting through a shared middleware chain on every protected endpoint. Public login, refresh, and health routes remain intentionally public; logout revokes a supplied refresh token.
+- Preserve the zero-runtime-dependency constraint and expose deterministic clocks/limits only as test injection points.
+
+## Shared interfaces and checkpoints
+
+- `createTokenManager({ secret, now, registry, accessTtlMs, refreshTtlMs })` is the sole token lifecycle boundary. It returns `issueTokenPair(user)`, `verifyAccessToken(token)`, `rotateRefreshToken(token)`, and `revokeRefreshToken(token)`. Pair responses are `{ accessToken, refreshToken, tokenType: "Bearer", expiresIn }`; stored registry keys are SHA-256 token digests and stored values contain metadata only.
+- `POST /login` accepts `{username,password}`; `POST /refresh` accepts `{refreshToken}`; `POST /logout` accepts `{refreshToken}`. Login/refresh return the pair shape above. Invalid refresh/replay returns 401. Logout is non-disclosing/idempotent at HTTP level and a valid supplied token can no longer rotate afterward. Invalid JSON returns 400.
+- `createAuthMiddleware({ tokenManager, getUser })` resolves the bearer `sub`, then reloads role/email from the user store (JWT role claims are never an authorization source). `createRateLimiter({ max, windowMs, now })` is keyed only after successful authentication. Server construction accepts one shared clock/token-manager/limiter graph.
+- Protected `GET /profile`, `GET /orders`, and `GET /admin` routes are declared through one `protectedEndpoint` composition boundary. `GET /health`, login, refresh, and logout are explicitly public lifecycle routes.
+- Producer checkpoint: after each T1/T2/T3 worker, that worker runs its contract command and records fresh output. Final adversarial checkpoint: an input-curated judge receives only requirements, current state, and contracts; it reruns every contract plus hostile off-contract probes. No task advances on a red producer checkpoint.
+
+```json agentfw-plan
+{
+  "version": "1.1",
+  "assurance": "A3",
+  "requirements": [
+    {"id": "R1", "text": "Extract all access/refresh token creation, parsing, signing, verification, revocation, and lifecycle constants into a dedicated token module."},
+    {"id": "R2", "text": "Add single-use refresh-token rotation with replay detection and token-family revocation."},
+    {"id": "R3", "text": "Replace cookie-backed sessions with bearer JWT access tokens and JWT refresh tokens; login, refresh, and logout expose the new lifecycle without sid cookies."},
+    {"id": "R4", "text": "Rate-limit authenticated requests per resolved user and return an explicit 429 response when that user's quota is exceeded without affecting another user."},
+    {"id": "R5", "text": "Route all protected API endpoints through shared authentication/authorization middleware while retaining the profile, orders, admin, health, and credential behaviors."}
+  ],
+  "tasks": [
+    {
+      "id": "T1",
+      "title": "Dedicated JWT token lifecycle and rotation registry",
+      "deps": [],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R1", "R2"],
+        "criteria": "The token module emits three-segment HS256 JWT pairs through the declared manager interface, rejects malformed/tampered/expired/wrong-type tokens at exact clock boundaries, atomically permits exactly one of simultaneous rotations, revokes all winning-token descendants after replay while preserving unrelated families, and stores only digests plus metadata.",
+        "acceptance_command": "node --test tests/tokens.test.js",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox; no network or socket binding",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "tampered, malformed, expired, and algorithm-confused JWTs are rejected",
+          "an access token cannot be used as a refresh token",
+          "two barrier-released rotations of one refresh token yield exactly one success",
+          "replay invalidates the winner and a later descendant while an unrelated family remains valid",
+          "tokens pass at exp minus one tick and fail exactly at exp",
+          "registry inspection finds digest keys and no raw access or refresh token substring in keys or values"
+        ],
+        "risk": "security and clock/concurrency semantics: refresh rotation must consume the old digest before issuing its replacement, expiration boundaries must fail closed, and raw refresh tokens must not be retained",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine Node test output produced_after_change",
+        "integration_seam": false,
+        "risk_class": "security",
+        "required_verification_tier": "adversarial",
+        "rerunnable": true,
+        "constraints": ["standard library only", "no network", "no plaintext token registry"]
+      }
+    },
+    {
+      "id": "T2",
+      "title": "Shared bearer authentication and per-user rate-limit middleware",
+      "deps": ["T1"],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R4", "R5"],
+        "criteria": "Middleware resolves only valid access bearer tokens to existing users, reloads authorization roles from the user store, authenticates before selecting a quota key, and counts requests in isolated per-user fixed windows with exact boundary and Retry-After behavior.",
+        "acceptance_command": "node --test tests/middleware.test.js",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox; deterministic injected clock and no socket binding",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "missing, malformed, refresh-type, and unknown-user bearer claims are unauthorized",
+          "a validly signed Alice token carrying an admin role claim remains forbidden because stored user role wins",
+          "forged/invalid Alice claims and unauthenticated traffic create no Alice quota state",
+          "one exhausted user's quota does not consume another user's quota",
+          "the final millisecond remains limited, exactly windowMs resets, and Retry-After matches the remaining rounded-up seconds"
+        ],
+        "risk": "security boundary and clock isolation: middleware ordering must authenticate before choosing a rate-limit key, and per-user counters must not become a global denial of service",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine Node test output produced_after_change",
+        "integration_seam": true,
+        "risk_class": "security",
+        "required_verification_tier": "adversarial",
+        "rerunnable": true,
+        "constraints": ["standard library only", "no IP-derived identity", "no network"]
+      }
+    },
+    {
+      "id": "T3",
+      "title": "JWT endpoint migration and full API integration",
+      "deps": ["T1", "T2"],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5"],
+        "criteria": "The declared login/refresh/logout shapes implement the JWT lifecycle without cookies; all three protected routes are constructed through the one shared middleware boundary; the whole suite proves prior token/middleware behavior still holds; architecture checks reject legacy session files, duplicate token logic, inline route authentication, skipped/empty tests, and stale cookie documentation.",
+        "acceptance_command": "./run-tests.sh",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox using an in-process request/response harness because listen(2) is denied",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "legacy sid cookies never authenticate and successful login emits no Set-Cookie header",
+          "replayed or revoked refresh tokens cannot mint access tokens",
+          "unauthorized, forbidden, and per-user over-limit requests return 401, 403, and 429 respectively",
+          "tampered or expired bearer JWTs fail on profile, orders, and admin",
+          "invalid JSON and wrong credentials preserve 400 and 401 behavior; health stays public",
+          "source checks require sessions.js removal, ban cookie/session/Set-Cookie and token lifecycle logic outside tokens.js, and require every protected route declaration to call protectedEndpoint",
+          "test inventory asserts named token, middleware, API, and architecture tests ran so empty or skipped files cannot pass",
+          "one injected fake clock drives issuance, verification, refresh, rate limiting, and the exact integration boundaries"
+        ],
+        "risk": "security integration seam across routing, body parsing, token lifecycle, authorization, rate limiting, and removal of legacy session bypasses",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine full test output and structural README/source search produced_after_change",
+        "integration_seam": true,
+        "risk_class": "security",
+        "required_verification_tier": "adversarial",
+        "rerunnable": true,
+        "constraints": ["standard library only", "no socket binding", "preserve unrelated user/order data"]
+      }
+    }
+  ]
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,123 @@
+# Authentication refactor plan
+
+## Capability preflight
+
+- Filesystem/permissions: the active session reports workspace-write with approval policy `never`; implementation is limited to this repository. Probe: the session permission profile plus `sed -n '1,240p' ~/.codex/config.toml` recorded the install default for comparison; the active managed sandbox supersedes that default.
+- Shell: active. Probe: `node --version` returned `v25.8.2`; baseline `./run-tests.sh` recorded `listen EPERM 127.0.0.1`, so tests must use an in-process HTTP request/response harness.
+- Isolated agents / independent review: active. Probe: two independent review-only subagents were successfully dispatched and returned separate C0-C5 verdicts.
+- Parallel agents: active, but writers share one worktree; implementation workers are serialized by dependency and path ownership.
+- Persistent state: this plan and test evidence are repository artifacts; no external task store is assumed.
+
+## Design decisions
+
+- Use compact, standards-shaped HS256 JWTs with explicit `access` and `refresh` token types. Access tokens are short-lived; refresh tokens are single-use and rotate into a new pair.
+- Keep refresh-token replay state in a dedicated token registry, keyed by a digest rather than raw token material. Reuse of a rotated token revokes its entire token family.
+- Remove cookie parsing, cookie issuance, and the server-side cookie session store from request authentication.
+- Apply authentication and per-user rate limiting through a shared middleware chain on every protected endpoint. Public login, refresh, and health routes remain intentionally public; logout revokes a supplied refresh token.
+- Preserve the zero-runtime-dependency constraint and expose deterministic clocks/limits only as test injection points.
+
+## Shared interfaces and checkpoints
+
+- `createTokenManager({ secret, now, registry, accessTtlMs, refreshTtlMs })` is the sole token lifecycle boundary. It returns `issueTokenPair(user)`, `verifyAccessToken(token)`, `rotateRefreshToken(token)`, and `revokeRefreshToken(token)`. Pair responses are `{ accessToken, refreshToken, tokenType: "Bearer", expiresIn }`; stored registry keys are SHA-256 token digests and stored values contain metadata only.
+- `POST /login` accepts `{username,password}`; `POST /refresh` accepts `{refreshToken}`; `POST /logout` accepts `{refreshToken}`. Login/refresh return the pair shape above. Invalid refresh/replay returns 401. Logout is non-disclosing/idempotent at HTTP level and a valid supplied token can no longer rotate afterward. Invalid JSON returns 400.
+- `createAuthMiddleware({ tokenManager, getUser })` resolves the bearer `sub`, then reloads role/email from the user store (JWT role claims are never an authorization source). `createRateLimiter({ max, windowMs, now })` is keyed only after successful authentication. Server construction accepts one shared clock/token-manager/limiter graph.
+- Protected `GET /profile`, `GET /orders`, and `GET /admin` routes are declared through one `protectedEndpoint` composition boundary. `GET /health`, login, refresh, and logout are explicitly public lifecycle routes.
+- Producer checkpoint: after each T1/T2/T3 worker, that worker runs its contract command and records fresh output. Final adversarial checkpoint: an input-curated judge receives only requirements, current state, and contracts; it reruns every contract plus hostile off-contract probes. No task advances on a red producer checkpoint.
+
+```json agentfw-plan
+{
+  "version": "1.1",
+  "assurance": "A3",
+  "requirements": [
+    {"id": "R1", "text": "Extract all access/refresh token creation, parsing, signing, verification, revocation, and lifecycle constants into a dedicated token module."},
+    {"id": "R2", "text": "Add single-use refresh-token rotation with replay detection and token-family revocation."},
+    {"id": "R3", "text": "Replace cookie-backed sessions with bearer JWT access tokens and JWT refresh tokens; login, refresh, and logout expose the new lifecycle without sid cookies."},
+    {"id": "R4", "text": "Rate-limit authenticated requests per resolved user and return an explicit 429 response when that user's quota is exceeded without affecting another user."},
+    {"id": "R5", "text": "Route all protected API endpoints through shared authentication/authorization middleware while retaining the profile, orders, admin, health, and credential behaviors."}
+  ],
+  "tasks": [
+    {
+      "id": "T1",
+      "title": "Dedicated JWT token lifecycle and rotation registry",
+      "deps": [],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R1", "R2"],
+        "criteria": "The token module emits three-segment HS256 JWT pairs through the declared manager interface, rejects malformed/tampered/expired/wrong-type tokens at exact clock boundaries, atomically permits exactly one of simultaneous rotations, revokes all winning-token descendants after replay while preserving unrelated families, and stores only digests plus metadata.",
+        "acceptance_command": "node --test tests/tokens.test.js",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox; no network or socket binding",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "tampered, malformed, expired, and algorithm-confused JWTs are rejected",
+          "an access token cannot be used as a refresh token",
+          "two barrier-released rotations of one refresh token yield exactly one success",
+          "replay invalidates the winner and a later descendant while an unrelated family remains valid",
+          "tokens pass at exp minus one tick and fail exactly at exp",
+          "registry inspection finds digest keys and no raw access or refresh token substring in keys or values"
+        ],
+        "risk": "security and clock/concurrency semantics: refresh rotation must consume the old digest before issuing its replacement, expiration boundaries must fail closed, and raw refresh tokens must not be retained",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine Node test output produced_after_change",
+        "integration_seam": false,
+        "risk_class": "security",
+        "required_verification_tier": "adversarial",
+        "rerunnable": true,
+        "constraints": ["standard library only", "no network", "no plaintext token registry"]
+      }
+    },
+    {
+      "id": "T2",
+      "title": "Shared bearer authentication and per-user rate-limit middleware",
+      "deps": ["T1"],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R4", "R5"],
+        "criteria": "Middleware resolves only valid access bearer tokens to existing users, reloads authorization roles from the user store, authenticates before selecting a quota key, and counts requests in isolated per-user fixed windows with exact boundary and Retry-After behavior.",
+        "acceptance_command": "node --test tests/middleware.test.js",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox; deterministic injected clock and no socket binding",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "missing, malformed, refresh-type, and unknown-user bearer claims are unauthorized",
+          "a validly signed Alice token carrying an admin role claim remains forbidden because stored user role wins",
+          "forged/invalid Alice claims and unauthenticated traffic create no Alice quota state",
+          "one exhausted user's quota does not consume another user's quota",
+          "the final millisecond remains limited, exactly windowMs resets, and Retry-After matches the remaining rounded-up seconds"
+        ],
+        "risk": "security boundary and clock isolation: middleware ordering must authenticate before choosing a rate-limit key, and per-user counters must not become a global denial of service",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine Node test output produced_after_change",
+        "integration_seam": true,
+        "risk_class": "security",
+        "required_verification_tier": "adversarial",
+        "rerunnable": true,
+        "constraints": ["standard library only", "no IP-derived identity", "no network"]
+      }
+    },
+    {
+      "id": "T3",
+      "title": "JWT endpoint migration and full API integration",
+      "deps": ["T1", "T2"],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5"],
+        "criteria": "The declared login/refresh/logout shapes implement the JWT lifecycle without cookies; all three protected routes are constructed through the one shared middleware boundary; the whole suite proves prior token/middleware behavior still holds; architecture checks reject legacy session files, duplicate token logic, inline route authentication, skipped/empty tests, and stale cookie documentation.",
+        "acceptance_command": "./run-tests.sh",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox using an in-process request/response harness because listen(2) is denied",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "legacy sid cookies never authenticate and successful login emits no Set-Cookie header",
+          "replayed or revoked refresh tokens cannot mint access tokens",
+          "unauthorized, forbidden, and per-user over-limit requests return 401, 403, and 429 respectively",
+          "tampered or expired bearer JWTs fail on profile, orders, and admin",
+          "invalid JSON and wrong credentials preserve 400 and 401 behavior; health stays public",
+          "source checks require sessions.js removal, ban cookie/session/Set-Cookie and token lifecycle logic outside tokens.js, and require every protected route declaration to call protectedEndpoint",
+          "test inventory asserts named token, middleware, API, and architecture tests ran so empty or skipped files cannot pass",
+          "one injected fake clock drives issuance, verification, refresh, rate limiting, and the exact integration boundaries"
+        ],
+        "risk": "security integration seam across routing, body parsing, token lifecycle, authorization, rate limiting, and removal of legacy session bypasses",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine full test output and structural README/source search produced_after_change",
+        "integration_seam": true,
+        "risk_class": "security",
+        "required_verification_tier": "adversarial",

+# Authentication refactor plan
+
+## Capability preflight
+
+- Filesystem/permissions: the active session reports workspace-write with approval policy `never`; implementation is limited to this repository. Probe: the session permission profile plus `sed -n '1,240p' ~/.codex/config.toml` recorded the install default for comparison; the active managed sandbox supersedes that default.
+- Shell: active. Probe: `node --version` returned `v25.8.2`; baseline `./run-tests.sh` recorded `listen EPERM 127.0.0.1`, so tests must use an in-process HTTP request/response harness.
+- Isolated agents / independent review: active. Probe: two independent review-only subagents were successfully dispatched and returned separate C0-C5 verdicts.
+- Parallel agents: active, but writers share one worktree; implementation workers are serialized by dependency and path ownership.
+- Persistent state: this plan and test evidence are repository artifacts; no external task store is assumed.
+
+## Design decisions
+
+- Use compact, standards-shaped HS256 JWTs with explicit `access` and `refresh` token types. Access tokens are short-lived; refresh tokens are single-use and rotate into a new pair.
+- Keep refresh-token replay state in a dedicated token registry, keyed by a digest rather than raw token material. Reuse of a rotated token revokes its entire token family.
+- Remove cookie parsing, cookie issuance, and the server-side cookie session store from request authentication.
+- Apply authentication and per-user rate limiting through a shared middleware chain on every protected endpoint. Public login, refresh, and health routes remain intentionally public; logout revokes a supplied refresh token.
+- Preserve the zero-runtime-dependency constraint and expose deterministic clocks/limits only as test injection points.
+
+## Shared interfaces and checkpoints
+
+- `createTokenManager({ secret, now, registry, accessTtlMs, refreshTtlMs })` is the sole token lifecycle boundary. It returns `issueTokenPair(user)`, `verifyAccessToken(token)`, `rotateRefreshToken(token)`, and `revokeRefreshToken(token)`. Pair responses are `{ accessToken, refreshToken, tokenType: "Bearer", expiresIn }`; stored registry keys are SHA-256 token digests and stored values contain metadata only.
+- `POST /login` accepts `{username,password}`; `POST /refresh` accepts `{refreshToken}`; `POST /logout` accepts `{refreshToken}`. Login/refresh return the pair shape above. Invalid refresh/replay returns 401. Logout is non-disclosing/idempotent at HTTP level and a valid supplied token can no longer rotate afterward. Invalid JSON returns 400.
+- `createAuthMiddleware({ tokenManager, getUser })` resolves the bearer `sub`, then reloads role/email from the user store (JWT role claims are never an authorization source). `createRateLimiter({ max, windowMs, now })` is keyed only after successful authentication. Server construction accepts one shared clock/token-manager/limiter graph.
+- Protected `GET /profile`, `GET /orders`, and `GET /admin` routes are declared through one `protectedEndpoint` composition boundary. `GET /health`, login, refresh, and logout are explicitly public lifecycle routes.
+- Producer checkpoint: after each T1/T2/T3 worker, that worker runs its contract command and records fresh output. Final adversarial checkpoint: an input-curated judge receives only requirements, current state, and contracts; it reruns every contract plus hostile off-contract probes. No task advances on a red producer checkpoint.
+
+```json agentfw-plan
+{
+  "version": "1.1",
+  "assurance": "A3",
+  "requirements": [
+    {"id": "R1", "text": "Extract all access/refresh token creation, parsing, signing, verification, revocation, and lifecycle constants into a dedicated token module."},
+    {"id": "R2", "text": "Add single-use refresh-token rotation with replay detection and token-family revocation."},
+    {"id": "R3", "text": "Replace cookie-backed sessions with bearer JWT access tokens and JWT refresh tokens; login, refresh, and logout expose the new lifecycle without sid cookies."},
+    {"id": "R4", "text": "Rate-limit authenticated requests per resolved user and return an explicit 429 response when that user's quota is exceeded without affecting another user."},
+    {"id": "R5", "text": "Route all protected API endpoints through shared authentication/authorization middleware while retaining the profile, orders, admin, health, and credential behaviors."}
+  ],
+  "tasks": [
+    {
+      "id": "T1",
+      "title": "Dedicated JWT token lifecycle and rotation registry",
+      "deps": [],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R1", "R2"],
+        "criteria": "The token module emits three-segment HS256 JWT pairs through the declared manager interface, rejects malformed/tampered/expired/wrong-type tokens at exact clock boundaries, atomically permits exactly one of simultaneous rotations, revokes all winning-token descendants after replay while preserving unrelated families, and stores only digests plus metadata.",
+        "acceptance_command": "node --test tests/tokens.test.js",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox; no network or socket binding",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "tampered, malformed, expired, and algorithm-confused JWTs are rejected",
+          "an access token cannot be used as a refresh token",
+          "two barrier-released rotations of one refresh token yield exactly one success",
+          "replay invalidates the winner and a later descendant while an unrelated family remains valid",
+          "tokens pass at exp minus one tick and fail exactly at exp",
+          "registry inspection finds digest keys and no raw access or refresh token substring in keys or values"
+        ],
+        "risk": "security and clock/concurrency semantics: refresh rotation must consume the old digest before issuing its replacement, expiration boundaries must fail closed, and raw refresh tokens must not be retained",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine Node test output produced_after_change",

+        "risk_class": "security",
+        "required_verification_tier": "adversarial",
+        "rerunnable": true,
+        "constraints": ["standard library only", "no network", "no plaintext token registry"]
+      }
+    },
+    {
+      "id": "T2",
+      "title": "Shared bearer authentication and per-user rate-limit middleware",
+      "deps": ["T1"],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R4", "R5"],
+        "criteria": "Middleware resolves only valid access bearer tokens to existing users, reloads authorization roles from the user store, authenticates before selecting a quota key, and counts requests in isolated per-user fixed windows with exact boundary and Retry-After behavior.",
+        "acceptance_command": "node --test tests/middleware.test.js",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox; deterministic injected clock and no socket binding",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "missing, malformed, refresh-type, and unknown-user bearer claims are unauthorized",
+          "a validly signed Alice token carrying an admin role claim remains forbidden because stored user role wins",
+          "forged/invalid Alice claims and unauthenticated traffic create no Alice quota state",
+          "one exhausted user's quota does not consume another user's quota",
+          "the final millisecond remains limited, exactly windowMs resets, and Retry-After matches the remaining rounded-up seconds"
+        ],
+        "risk": "security boundary and clock isolation: middleware ordering must authenticate before choosing a rate-limit key, and per-user counters must not become a global denial of service",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine Node test output produced_after_change",
+        "integration_seam": true,
+        "risk_class": "security",
+        "required_verification_tier": "adversarial",
+        "rerunnable": true,
+        "constraints": ["standard library only", "no IP-derived identity", "no network"]
+      }
+    },
+    {
+      "id": "T3",
+      "title": "JWT endpoint migration and full API integration",
+      "deps": ["T1", "T2"],
+      "contract": {
+        "requirement_ids": ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5"],
+        "criteria": "The declared login/refresh/logout shapes implement the JWT lifecycle without cookies; all three protected routes are constructed through the one shared middleware boundary; the whole suite proves prior token/middleware behavior still holds; architecture checks reject legacy session files, duplicate token logic, inline route authentication, skipped/empty tests, and stale cookie documentation.",
+        "acceptance_command": "./run-tests.sh",
+        "environment": "Node.js 25 in the managed workspace sandbox using an in-process request/response harness because listen(2) is denied",
+        "expected_signal": "process exits 0 and the Node test summary reports zero failures",
+        "negative_cases": [
+          "legacy sid cookies never authenticate and successful login emits no Set-Cookie header",
+          "replayed or revoked refresh tokens cannot mint access tokens",
+          "unauthorized, forbidden, and per-user over-limit requests return 401, 403, and 429 respectively",
+          "tampered or expired bearer JWTs fail on profile, orders, and admin",
+          "invalid JSON and wrong credentials preserve 400 and 401 behavior; health stays public",
+          "source checks require sessions.js removal, ban cookie/session/Set-Cookie and token lifecycle logic outside tokens.js, and require every protected route declaration to call protectedEndpoint",
+          "test inventory asserts named token, middleware, API, and architecture tests ran so empty or skipped files cannot pass",
+          "one injected fake clock drives issuance, verification, refresh, rate limiting, and the exact integration boundaries"

+        "risk": "security integration seam across routing, body parsing, token lifecycle, authorization, rate limiting, and removal of legacy session bypasses",
+        "evidence": "behavioral-machine full test output and structural README/source search produced_after_change",
+        "integration_seam": true,
+        "risk_class": "security",

+      }

+# Authentication refactor plan
+
+## Capability preflight
+
+- Filesystem/permissions: the active session reports workspace-write with approval policy `never`; implementation is limited to this repository. Probe: the session permission profile plus `sed -n '1,240p' ~/.codex/config.toml` recorded the install default for comparison; the active managed sandbox supersedes that default.
+- Shell: active. Probe: `node --version` returned `v25.8.2`; baseline `./run-tests.sh` recorded `listen EPERM 127.0.0.1`, so tests must use an in-process HTTP request/response harness.
+- Isolated agents / independent review: active. Probe: two independent review-only subagents were successfully dispatched and returned separate C0-C5 verdicts.
+- Parallel agents: active, but writers share one worktree; implementation workers are serialized by dependency and path ownership.
+- Persistent state: this plan and test evidence are repository artifacts; no external task store is assumed.
+
+## Design decisions
+
+- Use compact, standards-shaped HS256 JWTs with explicit `access` and `refresh` token types. Access tokens are short-lived; refresh tokens are single-use and rotate into a new pair.
+- Keep refresh-token replay state in a dedicated token registry, keyed by a digest rather than raw token material. Reuse of a rotated token revokes its entire token family.
+- Remove cookie parsing, cookie issuance, and the server-side cookie session store from request authentication.
+- Apply authentication and per-user rate limiting through a shared middleware chain on every protected endpoint. Public login, refresh, and health routes remain intentionally public; logout revokes a supplied refresh token.
+- Preserve the zero-runtime-dependency constraint and expose deterministic clocks/limits only as test injection points.
+
+## Shared interfaces and checkpoints
+
+- `createTokenManager({ secret, now, registry, accessTtlMs, refreshTtlMs })` is the sole token lifecycle boundary. It returns `issueTokenPair(user)`, `verifyAccessToken(token)`, `rotateRefreshToken(token)`, and `revokeRefreshToken(token)`. Pair responses are `{ accessToken, refreshToken, tokenType: "Bearer", expiresIn }`; stored registry keys are SHA-256 token digests and stored values contain metadata only.
+- `POST /login` accepts `{username,password}`; `POST /refresh` accepts `{refreshToken}`; `POST /logout` accepts `{refreshToken}`. Login/refresh return the pair shape above. Invalid refresh/replay returns 401. Logout is non-disclosing/idempotent at HTTP level and a valid supplied token can no longer rotate afterward. Invalid JSON returns 400.
+- `createAuthMiddleware({ tokenManager, getUser })` resolves the bearer `sub`, then reloads role/email from the user store (JWT role claims are never an authorization source). `createRateLimiter({ max, windowMs, now })` is keyed only after successful authentication. Server construction accepts one shared clock/token-manager/limiter graph.
+- Protected `GET /profile`, `GET /orders`, and `GET /admin` routes are declared through one `protectedEndpoint` composition boundary. `GET /health`, login, refresh, and logout are explicitly public lifecycle routes.
+- Producer checkpoint: after each T1/T2/T3 worker, that worker runs its contract command and records fresh output. Final adversarial checkpoint: an input-curated judge receives only requirements, current state, and contracts; it reruns every contract plus hostile off-contract probes. No task advances on a red producer checkpoint.
+
